newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori says hopes for peaceful siege end.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says hopes for peaceful siege end.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said on Tuesday he hoped for a bloodless solution to the three-week-old Lima hostage crisis.
"Like everyone, I hope for a peaceful solution," Fujimori told reporters during a surprise visit to a Lima shantytown.

The president, who had stopped his regular visits to the capital's shantytowns when the crisis broke, added: "The life of the hostages is assured -- their physical well-being -- because there are not going to be acts of blood. Fortunately this is being achieved."
"We should not transmit the image that in Peru we are living a situation of terrorism," he said.

Asked what his current position was in the crisis, he replied: "A mixture of firmness in our position -- and in this sense the non-liberation of MRTA (Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement) prisoners -- and at the same time prudence."
The rebels are demanding the government free all their 400-plus jailed comrades in return for the release of their 74 hostages.
